summary: Marion County ground site: L-4 cab built 1934 on the Willamette NF, staffed in 1941, burned in October 1968; no source describes the summit today.

facts.status_note: Gone by 1968; Forest Lookouts says the structure was disposed of by burning on October 11, 1968.

events.note: Named one of eleven new emergency lookout stations; to be linked by the forest telephone system to the fire control office at Fish Lake.
L-4 cab built in 1934. The register says the USFS built it; Forest Lookouts says the CCC constructed a 14x14 L-4 lookout house.
Newspaper of July 31, 1934 names Kenneth Wilson as stationed at the lookout, 6,035 ft, highest in the Willamette National Forest.
Staffed for 70 days; reports ran through the Detroit Ranger Station by way of the Santiam Co-op Telephone Company.
Structure disposed of by burning on October 11, 1968. The register says it was gone by 1968.
Registered August 16, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the USFS built the 1934 L-4 cab; Forest Lookouts says the CCC constructed a 14x14 L-4 lookout house. The story reports both and does not pick one.
The register gives 6,043 ft (1,842 m); Forest Lookouts quotes a 1934 newspaper at 6,035 ft. The record keeps the register's 1,841.9 m.

notes_for_editor: The brief's firelookout.com link for this site (https://www.firelookout.com/or/bearpoint.html) returns a page for the Eagle Rock Fire Lookout Cabin (Willamette NF, Marion County, 1934 L-5 cab, gone 1953), not Bear Point. It was not used, and the record's source list should drop that URL or point it at the correct page. A Forest Service page and an AllTrails listing for a Bear Point summit trail (Trail #3342, one labelled closed) came up in search; neither was read in full and neither is used, so visit and access facts are omitted. The brief's design (L-4), county, agency and elevation (1,841.9 m) are confirmed; no corrections proposed.
